status_summary: On 2025-12-04 the USPTO Director issued a memorandum to the examining corps on subject matter eligibility declarations and a companion memorandum to applicants on best practices for filing them; the corps memorandum says it creates no new practice. On 2025-12-05 the Deputy Commissioner for Patents issued an advance notice revising MPEP sections 2106.04 and 2106.05 to incorporate the precedential Ex Parte Desjardins decision, effective on issuance. The Patent Eligibility Restoration Act of 2025, which would rewrite Section 101, was introduced on 2025-05-01 in the House (H.R. 3152) and in the Senate (S. 1546, Senators Tillis and Coons), each referred to its Judiciary Committee. The statutory text of Section 101 is unchanged. On 2026-07-14 the Senate Judiciary Committee held a full-committee hearing on patent eligibility; the committee page names no bill, and Tech Times describes the hearing as one on the Senate bill and as a possible precursor to a markup. No committee vote or floor action was found.

timeline.event: The Patent Eligibility Restoration Act of 2025 (H.R. 3152) was introduced in the House and referred to the Judiciary Committee; it would rewrite Section 101 with a list of exclusions.
The Patent Eligibility Restoration Act of 2025 (S. 1546) was introduced in the Senate by Senator Tillis with Senator Coons and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

The USPTO Director issued a memorandum to the patent examining corps on subject matter eligibility declarations under Rule 132, and a companion memorandum to applicants and practitioners on best practices for submitting them.
The Deputy Commissioner for Patents issued an advance notice of changes to MPEP sections 2106.04 and 2106.05 incorporating the precedential Ex Parte Desjardins decision, effective on issuance.

The Senate Judiciary Committee held a full-committee hearing titled "From Genes to Machines: The Patent Eligibility Debate" at 10:15 a.m. in Hart Senate Office Building Room 216, with four listed witnesses, including a former USPTO Director; the committee page names no bill.
timeline.source: U.S. Senate Committee on the Judiciary

title: Re-examine Section 101 patent eligibility for emerging technologies
uncertainties: The corps memorandum states that it does not create new practice, so its weight as reform is limited; the MPEP revision is the operative change. The Senate hearing of 2026-07-14 is listed on the committee page, which names no bill; the link to the Patent Eligibility Restoration Act rests on Tech Times coverage. The Senate bill (S. 1546) was read in its introduced text on GovInfo, but the later status of S. 1546 and H.R. 3152 was not retrieved from congress.gov, and searches through 2026-11-02 found no markup or vote. The Mandate also asks for a balanced approach to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board; the USPTO published proposed rules on Board practice on 2025-10-17 (Federal Register), which this record does not assess. Other 2025 eligibility guidance, such as any earlier memoranda on artificial intelligence claims, was not reviewed. Searches through 2026-11-02 found no USPTO eligibility guidance issued after the December 2025 memoranda, though law-firm commentary on those memoranda continued into 2026.
